strengths: Novel problem formulation identifying an underexplored security vulnerability in VLMs for visual grounding tasks with realistic, well-motivated attack scenarios
Clever technical approach using text-conditional U-Net to generate semantic triggers adaptively based on target object descriptions
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across three VLMs and four datasets with thorough ablation studies, transferability analysis, and defense evaluation
Strong empirical results achieving 65-71% ASR@0.5 on InternVL-2.5-8B with minimal clean accuracy degradation (1-3%)
Theoretical analysis providing existence and convergence guarantees despite strong assumptions
Well-presented paper with clear motivation and effective visualizations of attack mechanism and impact
weaknesses: Threat model assumes white-box access during fine-tuning (supply-chain attack), limiting practical applicability; detectability during training and deployment not addressed

Attack success rates drop substantially on grounding-specialized models (40-50% for Ferret-7B, 29-46% for COCO-2017), which are primary deployment targets; explanation in Section 7 insufficiently justifies why rates should be much lower than fixed-target attacks

Theoretical analysis relies on extremely strong, empirically unvalidated assumptions: universal approximation capability, fixed trigger pattern uniqueness, and data separability; existence proof does not guarantee joint optimization finds solutions
Imperceptibility not rigorously validated—no quantitative metrics, user studies, or systematic evaluation of whether smooth L1 reconstruction loss is sufficient across diverse image types
Limited defense discussion: Table 3 shows existing defenses fail without explaining why or proposing IAG-specific countermeasures; no discussion of potential solutions like adversarial training
Baseline comparisons limited (acknowledged lack of direct baselines); comparison with simplified BadEncoder/TrojVLM in Table 2 unfair due to different problem formulation
Real-world experiments only show 7 cherry-picked examples without systematic evaluation on diverse images or human validation of success
Incomplete ablations: no isolation of text-conditional U-Net contribution; hyperparameter β set 'empirically' without sensitivity analysis; reconstruction loss weight impact unexplored
Transferability shows degradation between datasets, especially to RefCocog, suggesting potential overfitting to specific datasets; generalization to new VLM architectures unclear
Code not available for reproducibility; implementation details unclear (text embedding integration into cross-attention); numbering errors throughout (multiple 'Equation (0)' references)

strengths: Novel and practical problem: First multi-target backdoor attack on VLM-based visual grounding, addressing a realistic threat where previous static-trigger attacks are unsuitable
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Five datasets, three VLM architectures, extensive ablations, defense evaluations, transferability analysis, and real-world examples
Strong empirical results: Achieves highest ASR in 11/12 settings (11.9%-32.8% improvement over baselines) while maintaining <3% benign accuracy drop and minimal inference overhead
Thorough imperceptibility analysis: PSNR 31-32 dB (above perceptual threshold), low L1/LPIPS scores, with visual demonstration of trigger naturalness
Well-executed presentation: Clear methodology, good visualizations, comprehensive supplementary material with hyperparameters and implementation details
Robustness against existing defenses: Demonstrates IAG evades Spectral Signature, Beatrix, PAR, and adaptive defenses
Practical effectiveness: Attack remains effective at 1% poison rate, demonstrating efficiency
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Text-conditioned UNet is from existing diffusion models; joint loss combining reconstruction and LM loss is straightforward; primary contribution is application rather than methodological innovation
Weak theoretical analysis: Assumptions A1-A3 lack empirical validation; bounds are loose; no proof that assumptions actually hold; informal explanation of why input-aware triggers help
Significant performance gaps on complex tasks: ShowUI ASR only 25-35%, COCO-2017 ASR 40-47%, limiting practical threat credibility despite justification about unseen objects

Incomplete baseline comparison: Most baselines adapted from classification tasks; VLM-specific baselines (BadVLMDriver, TrojVLM, VLOOD) achieving 42-48% ASR relegated to Appendix J, contradicting main paper dismissal of 'ASR ≈ 0'
Mixed transferability results: RefCoco→RefCocog transfer shows significant drop (50.2%→60.3%), suggesting limited robustness to distribution shift; VQA transfer uses ethically problematic hate speech
No proposed defenses or mitigations: Thoroughly critiques attacks but offers no solutions or future defense directions, limiting constructive impact for security research

Hyperparameter selection inadequately justified: β=0.5 chosen despite Table 9 showing β=0.1 achieves slightly higher ASR; α₁, α₂ follow general recommendations without dataset-specific validation; max token lengths appear ad-hoc
Limited failure case analysis: No systematic investigation of which object types are harder to attack, or how ASR correlates with object similarity to training targets

Real-world evaluation not systematic: Only example-based results; screenshots appear manually created rather than from live systems; no evaluation on actual GUI agents or embodied AI systems mentioned in motivation
Suspicious defense results: Table 4 shows Beatrix defense increases ASR (50.2%→54.2% on RefCocog), counter-intuitive result without explanation suggesting possible experimental issue
